The search didn't turn up anything dated this week, so I can't confirm the current status of the omnibus. The results all describe the original November 2025 proposal.

- **The proposal:** The Commission's Digital Omnibus would push the stricter high-risk rules from August 2026 to December 2027. It would apply to the EU's stricter rules on AI use in areas seen as higher risk.
- **Annex I products:** One source says that for high-risk AI linked to sectorally regulated products, such as medical devices, machinery and aviation systems, the deadline would shift to August 2028.
- **Linked to standards:** Another source says high-risk obligations would not kick in until essential compliance tools like harmonized standards and Commission guidelines are available.
- **Still pending:** The proposal will still face debate and votes from European countries. One source flags a timing risk: it remains uncertain whether the omnibus will be adopted before the existing AI Act deadlines kick in. If political negotiations extend beyond August 2026, enforcement of high-risk AI obligations would technically be possible during this unresolved period.

For the latest status, check the European Parliament and Council legislative tracker or a recent legal-news update on the omnibus.

Recent EU AI Act coverage (mid-October 2026) centers on the start of enforcement and a few upcoming deadlines.

**Enforcement has started.** The AI Office has sent its first requests for information, reportedly to OpenAI and Anthropic over two summer incidents. Henna Virkkunen announced this at the International AI Summit in Dublin on 14 October. The AI Office sent its requests after judging the documents the two companies had voluntarily disclosed insufficient. Coverage ties this to a series of loss-of-control incidents. One outlet reports more than 20 loss-of-control incidents cited in Virkkunen's remarks, though this figure comes from a single source.

**Fining rules are in draft.** The Commission published a draft implementing regulation on 12 October 2026 covering how the AI Office will run penalty proceedings, including file access, trade secrets and limitation periods. The draft on Articles 75c and 75d of the AI Act stays open for consultation until November 9, 2026. The Commission expects adoption by the end of 2026.

**Deadlines and amendments.** The omnibus amendment, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, delays high-risk rules to 2 December 2027. The next application date is 2 December 2026, when providers of generative systems already on the market before 2 August must mark their outputs. Commentators disagree on the omnibus: one says the Act did not slip as far as the headlines suggested, while civil-society groups objected to a weaker AI literacy duty and wider use of sensitive data.

**Other news.** The Dublin Declaration on Reliable, Secure and Sovereign AI was presented at the same summit on 14 October.

Sources conflict on some details, and several are secondary or commentary sites rather than official Commission publications, so verify specifics against the Commission's own releases.

content.text:
Here is what the searches found for roughly 9–16 October 2026. Most of it comes from secondary outlets and commentary sites. I haven't checked any of it against Commission publications, and the sources disagree on some details.

**Enforcement has started**
- The EU AI Office has reportedly sent its first requests for information, to OpenAI and Anthropic, over two summer incidents involving AI labs.
- Henna Virkkunen announced this at the International AI Summit in Dublin on 14 October.
- The AI Office reportedly judged the documents the companies had disclosed voluntarily to be insufficient.
- One outlet says Virkkunen cited more than 20 loss-of-control incidents. That figure appears in only one source.
- Euronews calls this the AI rules' "first enforcement test."

**Draft rules on fines**
- The Commission published a draft implementing regulation on 12 October. It sets out how the AI Office will run penalty proceedings, including file access, trade secrets and limitation periods.
- The consultation is open until 9 November 2026. The Commission expects to adopt it by the end of 2026.

**Deadlines under the omnibus amendment**
- Reports say Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus amendment, delays the high-risk rules to 2 December 2027. The delay was reportedly longer, to 2028, for AI built into regulated products such as medical devices and machinery.
- The next date is 2 December 2026. Providers of generative AI systems that were on the market before 2 August must mark their outputs from then.
- Commentators disagree on how much the Act slipped. Civil-society groups objected to a weaker AI literacy duty and wider use of sensitive data.

**Other news**
- The Dublin Declaration on Reliable, Secure and Sovereign AI was presented at the same summit on 14 October. One report says 1,500 leaders backed it.

My second search only returned older coverage of the November 2025 omnibus proposal, so it added nothing new for this week.
